experiments.why: A value f32 cannot hold exactly, so lo carries the nonzero remainder that the df64_mul cross terms depend on.
2^24+1, the first integer f32 cannot hold, so hi rounds to 16777216 and lo must be exactly 1.
An Earth-radius-scale literal, the typical fp64 value whose fraction lives only in lo.
The pinned slot the existing tests use, which must come back as group 2, binding 5.
A pin at the first slot, where an auto-injected default guard could otherwise appear as a second binding.

obligations.statement: splitF64(x) returns the pair [hi, lo] with hi = Math.fround(x) and lo = Math.fround(x - hi).
